A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SteeM research. Their full text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained content across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original human annotations, memory-anchoring measurements, trained-model evaluations, generalization tests, and comparative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds annotation-reliability measurements, alternative-judge evaluations, human controllability results, and pairwise model comparisons.

M1.justification: The data-generation and filtering procedure, supervised fine-tuning, GRPO objective, and reward components remain unchanged. SteeM-NL and SteeM-Tag rename the previously evaluated natural-language and tag-conditioned variants.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Research and Tutoring dataset, four task categories, Medical and Humanities generalization subjects, and AlpacaEval evaluation. The added validation studies do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 extends pairwise comparisons beyond the retained Memory Masking comparison to None, Rubric Instruct, and SFT-only SteeM in Table 8. These methods already appeared in scalar-score evaluations; their definitions remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 substantially expands validation design: 100 existing response pairs receive three human labels, judge backbones are varied, matched queries with different target preferences undergo human comparison, and additional baselines undergo pairwise evaluation. The original test split and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test inter-annotator reliability, consistency across scenarios and tasks, robustness to judge choice, and human perception of controllability. Table 8 also tests the RL contribution through pairwise preferences, supplementing the retained scalar SFT-versus-RL comparison.

E5.justification: Appendix G adds two further annotations for 100 previously annotated pairs and introduces Krippendorff's alpha, reporting 0.71 overall alongside subgroup agreement and unsure rates. Neither version reports model-seed variability or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: V2 adds several distinct quantitative findings: 80–85% human–judge agreement across judge backbones, human controllability agreement of 77% versus 65% for Qwen3-8B, and SteeM pairwise wins over SFT-only of 59.8% and 55.1% for 4B and 8B. Existing benchmark values and plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), the memory-dependence definitions, and the complete judging rubric are unchanged. The added low-, middle-, and high-score explanation in Section 3.2 restates the existing appendix rubric rather than revising the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about memory anchoring, user-controllable dependence, SteeM's alignment advantages, and preservation of response quality. The new studies provide additional support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 expands the interpretation of preference interfaces, emphasizing effects on general capabilities and usability. Sections 5.1.3 and 5.3 explain complementary pairwise validation and filtering versus generation control. The stated limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and explicitly identifies Gemini-2.5-Pro as the main memory-dependence judge in Table 7. Appendix B's training hyperparameters and the existing masking and judging prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged, as is the central positioning relative to alignment methods, personalization benchmarks, and memory-enhanced agents. Related-work wording edits do not substantively alter these relationships.

P1.justification: V2 expands the score explanation, rewrites Section 5.2, adds Section 5.1.3 and Appendix H, and updates terminology and cross-references. Author order and a corresponding-author marker also change. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 6–8, renumbers the former Tables 6–7 as Tables 9–10, and reflows existing material. Table 4's labels and Figure 7's caption receive limited edits. The original figure content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the existing evidence through overlapping annotations, alternative judges, human controllability checks, and broader pairwise comparisons; code-access information also helps reproducibility. The gain is limited by incomplete reporting: the new human controllability study leaves its sample size unstated, and Table 6's 83% overall agreement is unexplained alongside subgroup rates averaging 82%. These qualifications limit confidence without outweighing the added validation.
